title: MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250 m (MOD13Q1 v061)
description: 16-day composite NDVI and EVI at 250 m from the MODIS instrument on Terra, with red, NIR, blue and MIR surface reflectances, view/sun geometry, composite day of year, VI quality and pixel reliability layers. Distributed as HDF-EOS2 files on the MODIS sinusoidal tile grid by the NASA Land Processes DAAC.
purpose: A consistent vegetation-index time series for Algeria since February 2000, widely used for monitoring cereal-season vegetation, drought impacts on rangeland and cropland, and inter-annual greenness anomalies at regional scale.

spatial_extent.description: Global land, processed in MODIS Sinusoidal Tiling System tiles (hXXvYY); only tiles containing land are produced. Users must select the tiles covering Algeria (or use AppEEARS) and reproject/clip themselves.

temporal_extent.description: From 18 February 2000. The data catalog page states that Terra MODIS acquisitions will cease on 1 December 2026 and recommends transitioning to the VIIRS products VJ213A1 (primary) or VJ113A1 (secondary).

variables.description: Day of year of the selected observation (1–366).

variables.name: View zenith, sun zenith, relative azimuth angles
variables.description: Observation geometry of the selected pixel.

processing: Since Collection 6, the 250 m VI product ingests pre-composited 8-day MODIS Level-2G surface reflectance (corrected for molecular scattering, ozone absorption and aerosols). The 16-day composite is built with a Constrained View angle – Maximum Value Composite (CV-MVC), with a plain Maximum Value Composite as backup. Collection 6.1 makes no change to the science algorithm; differences from C6 come from Level-1B calibration and polarization-correction updates.
limitations: Terra MODIS acquisitions are scheduled to end on 1 December 2026 (per the NASA data catalog page), so the series will not continue beyond that date; continuity requires switching to VIIRS vegetation-index products.
250 m pixels mix fields, fallow and natural vegetation in fragmented landscapes; NDVI/EVI values are not crop-specific.
The maximum-value compositing selects one observation per 16-day period, so the actual observation date varies within the period (see Composite day of year).
Downloading requires a free NASA Earthdata Login account.

algeria_notes: Across northern Algeria's cereal and steppe zones, MOD13Q1 NDVI is a practical indicator of season greenness and drought stress, but 250 m pixels mix cereal fields, fallow, rangeland and orchards, so it should not be read as a crop-specific signal. Over the Sahara, NDVI stays near bare-soil values apart from oases and irrigated perimeters, which may occupy only part of a pixel.

verification.notes: DOI 10.5067/MODIS/MOD13Q1.061 confirmed via DataCite content negotiation (Didan, 2021; NASA LP DAAC; title 'MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061'). Earthdata Login requirement confirmed by a test request on a granule URL, which returned a 302 redirect to urs.earthdata.nasa.gov. The bbox is the global extent stated on the catalog page. The legacy lpdaac.usgs.gov product URL now redirects to earthdata.nasa.gov, and the old e4ftl01 data-pool path returned 404.

alert: NASA has announced that Terra MODIS acquisitions cease on 1 December 2026. The archive remains available, but the time series will not be extended; NASA points users to equivalent VIIRS products.
